newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Fate of Venezuela's Viasa airline hangs in balance.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Venezuela's Viasa airline hangs in balance.

text.p: Workers at struggling Venezuelan flag-carrying airline Viasa said they rejected restructuring plans by majority shareholder Iberia due to be considered at a crucial shareholders meeting set for Wednesday.
Iberia has proposed cutting routes and shedding some 20 percent of the 2,200 workforce.
It has also said it would capitalise some $35 million of Viasa's $140 million debts, increasing its shareholding from 45 to 100 percent.
With no preliminary agreement yet reached, the loss-making airline's fate hangs in the balance and "one can only wait," union representative to Viasa's executive board William Bracho, told Reuters.
However, "Iberia taking 100 percent control doesn't seem to us like a solution," Bracho said.
Iberia says Viasa, which has made continuing but falling losses totalling some $200 million over the past five years, could turn a $14 million profit if the restructuring plan is approved.
Iberia invested an initial $73.5 million to buy the airline in 1991, paid another $43.6 million in 1991 and 1992 to cover losses, and refuses to stump-up more.
But Bracho said Iberia had "sucked the airline of some $70 million every year and has not provided any real capital -- only usurious rates of interest."
"Viasa has been exploited by its majority owner at the cost of smaller shareholders and the Venezuelan government," he added.
Venezuela's National Investment Fund currently holds 40 percent of the airline.
